name: Finite Auxiliary with not

1.definition: Expresses clausal negation with not associated with the finite auxiliary.

projection.target: Not follows the finite auxiliary in an ordinary declarative, and lexical verbs generally require do in this frame. Nonfinite negation places not differently.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Where not goes in a sentence
curious.summary: In an ordinary statement, not comes right after the first helping verb.
curious.body: In She has not received it, the word not follows has. The helping verb has is the finite one, and not attaches to it to make the whole clause negative. This dictionary also says that verbs like receive generally need do in this kind of sentence when there's no other helping verb, and that when the verb has no tense, not goes elsewhere. This dictionary marks the account as provisional.
curious.try: Take a statement with a helping verb, such as She has finished. Where does not go to make it negative?

teacher.summary: Shows where not sits relative to the finite auxiliary in a negative statement.
teacher.explain: In an ordinary declarative, not follows the finite auxiliary: She has not received it. Lexical verbs generally require do in this frame, and nonfinite negation places not differently. This dictionary treats not as associated with the finite auxiliary, expressing clausal negation. It marks the analysis as provisional and the example is constructed, so use it as a starting pattern rather than a full account of negation.
teacher.terms: This dictionary's term for the verb that not follows is finite auxiliary.
watch_for: A learner might place not before the auxiliary instead of after it.
A learner might negate a lexical verb directly with not, without do.
teacher.activity: Give students affirmative sentences with has, is and will. They rewrite each as negative and underline the finite auxiliary and the not that follows it.

child.hook: Where does the word not go when you say you haven't done something?
child.explain: Look at She has not received it. The little word not comes right after has. A helper word like has comes first, and not follows it.
child.play: Pick a sentence with a helper word, such as She has finished. Make it say the opposite by adding not. Say where you put it.

checked.note: Audit: fixed teacher.terms, cutting primary auxiliary (such as have, be, do), since the entry covers any finite auxiliary and the activity uses will. Also replaced the entry with this dictionary in curious and teacher text, and the curious body now says receive needs do when there is no other helping verb.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Finite Auxiliary with not." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/primary-auxiliary-negation-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
